Hi Ethan / Rachel,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached is our reference design (redwood-apexline-reference-design-v1.pdf) and a lightweight checklist we use for partner solution assurance. The goal for this thread: agree on a small validation matrix, confirm data paths (payload shapes + residency), and schedule a 4-hour validation window next week.

Key asks to unblock validation:
- Confirm a sample payload set (anonymized) or synthetic generator we can use.
- Clarify which ApexLine service endpoints will call Redwood hosted API vs. Dedicated/private.
- Any additional compliance constraints (e.g., no external logging for PII flows).

Proposed validation scope (short):
1) Functional flow: end-to-end request -> predict -> post-process (sanity checks)
2) Latency SLO smoke: 95th pct < 150ms on 1kQPS simulated bursts for short sequences (<=128 tokens)
3) Throughput: multi-conn burst behavior w/ caching off/on
4) Error mode: simulate model failover and confirm fallback mapping

Please reply with the sample data approach and preferred validation windows. If you want, Marissa and Jonas will join the call to walk the runbook.

Thanks,
Sergio Alvarez
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Sergio — thanks, received the reference design.

Quick summary of what we ran today (attached validation-results-20261013.csv):
- Baseline functional checks passed for simple prompts.
- Observed increased tail latency when KV cache was disabled (we tested simulating multiple unique sessions).
- One failure mode: streaming chunk order mismatch under small packet MTU; happened intermittently at ~0.5% requests.

Open questions for Redwood:
- For private deployments, what is the expected behavior of the prefix/KV cache when clients rotate API keys frequently?
- Do you provide a recommended model-variant mapping list (e.g., alpine-3b -> redwood-3b-int8) for our latency/accuracy tradeoffs?

We can produce anonymized payloads by EOD tomorrow. Preferred validation window is Oct 14 13:00–17:00 PDT. Can Marissa be the technical contact during the run?

—Ethan

Ethan — great, thanks for the quick validation run and the CSV. Answers inline below and a short mutual action plan.

- KV cache + key rotation: By default Redwood ties prefix/KV cache to a session token rather than API key; rapid API key rotation at the auth layer will not evict prefix entries unless the session token changes. For Private deployments with strict key rotation policies we recommend using session affinity or our session token passthrough (see p.12 of the reference design).

- Model-variant mapping: Attached is a short mapping suggestion (embedded in the reference PDF) but quick guidance:
  * short sequences, latency-critical: redwood-3b-int8 or redwood-7b-q4f for cost/latency sweet spot
  * high-quality long-context: redwood-13b or higher, prefer dedicated pools

Mutual action plan (short):
1) ApexLine to share anonymized payload set by Oct 13 EOD — Ethan
2) Redwood to prep validation environment and runbook, instrument prefix cache toggles — Marissa & Jonas
3) Joint validation window: Oct 14 13:00–17:00 PDT — all
4) Post-run action: collect traces, confirm fallback mapping for any observed failovers — Laura

Marissa — can you confirm instrumentation steps (sampling, traces, which logs we need turned on) and whether we can reproduce the streaming chunk ordering locally?

Thanks,
Sergio
